g.text: How a quote is produced — the three core flows
Every job enters the SAME front door (Step 0), then the operator sends it down ONE of three lanes.
STEP 0 · SHARED ENTRY — every job starts the same way

text.tspan: Not here: no strength / crush check yet, no distance, no van choice, no price.
The front door only reads and labels the PDF.

g.text: LANE A · POINT-TO-POINT (one pickup → one drop, in our own vans)

text.tspan: Not here: no extra stops, no shared truck, no drop-order zoning.
The return trip is estimated as ×2 the outbound, not re-measured.

g.text: LANE B · MULTI-STOP (one van, an ordered chain of stops)

text.tspan: Not here: no mixed pickup-and-drop 'milk run', no re-packing per stop.
It reuses the already-packed vans and Lane A's price engine.

g.text: LANE C · GROUPAGE (many companies share the same trucks, via hubs)

text.tspan: Not here: no spreadsheet import; price is flat per pallet-space (no mileage, no 3-D volume).
Only hub-routed quotes can be booked. Records are flat JSON files, not a database.
0.1 Receive the upload
(read the raw PDF bytes; nothing checked yet)
0.2 Check the file is safe
(size limit + proof it is really a PDF)
0.3 Read the pages
(the PDF's own text first; OCR only if scanned)
0.4 Build the cargo tables
(only proper grid tables are picked up)
0.5 Archive the source
(optional — off by default)
0.6 Tag each item fragile or standard
(keyword rules; unsure → flag for review)
0.7 Find pickup & delivery addresses
(read only — not yet checked on a map)
0.8 Derive routing hints
(stop numbers, collect-vs-deliver; all advisory)
0.9 Hand back one structured result
(no price yet, no mode chosen)

g.text: The default lane. Used when the job has just one drop.

text.tspan: A.1 Receive the cargo & validate
(sane sizes and whole quantities)
A.2 Assemble the load units
(real 3-D items + durability / which-way-up)
A.3 Optional bulk consolidation
(off by default; huge lists → placeable blocks)
A.4 Pack in 3-D & rank the vans
(tries orientations, respects reach height)
A.5 Pick the cheapest set of vans
(overflow is shown, never silently dropped)
A.6 Independently re-check the plan is safe
(a bad plan is blocked, not shipped)
A.7 Measure the drive: one pickup → one drop
(Google Maps, or straight-line if no key)
A.8 Build the price
(round-trip miles + fuel + driver time + fragile fee)

g.text: A.9 Save the quote (and optionally email it)

text.tspan: Two shapes: 1 pickup + many drops (delivery)
or a depot + many pickups (collection)

g.text: B.1 Operator builds the ordered stop list

text.tspan: B.2 Validate the request
(every stop needs an address + valid kind)
B.3 Stop-mix rule check
(clear error naming the bad stop + the fix)
B.4 Route the whole chain in one call
(one-way; no return leg billed for delivery)
B.5 Distance via Google, or straight-line fallback
(fallback keeps the typed order)
B.6 Work out the visited order
(collection proves each pickup appears once)
B.7 Price the trip
(reuses Lane A's engine + per-stop handling)
B.8 Add hub fees & advisory flags
(flags never block a stop)
C.1 Hub network is set up (prerequisite)
(11 UK hubs, each owns postcode areas)
C.2 Read the manifest into draft consignments
(several companies' part-loads at once)
C.3 Parse the collection-run table offline
(pallet count + size; no AI, no network)
C.4 Read / calculate per-pallet weight
(trusted or worked out — never guessed)
C.5 Collapse hub double-counting
(one trunk load; only when the two legs match)
C.6 Overlay the manifest's own hubs
(this session only; widen the catchment)
C.7 Quote one consignment
(hubs → demand → path → capacity → price)
C.8 Capacity — a configurable ceiling
(soft weight cap; hard truck-leg stop)
C.9 Group loads onto shared trucks + 3-D plan
(auto-splits across trucks when over capacity)
C.10 Book it: server re-quote + anti-drift
(re-price on the server; lock the total)
C.11 Track the shipment through its lifecycle
(booked → collected → in transit → delivered)
C.12 Per-leg load view & on-demand hub distance
(read-only; enforces nothing)
